arxiv-1409-7606.title: Positively Curved Manifolds with Large Spherical Rank Thanks: The first named author is partially supported by the NSF grant DMS–1207655. The second named author is partially supported by the NSF grant DMS–1104352. The third named author is partially supported by the NSF grant DMS–1307164.
arxiv-1409-7606.creator: Benjamin Schmidt, Krishnan Shankar, Ralf Spatzier
arxiv-1409-7606.description: Abstract . Rigidity results are obtained for Riemannian d d -manifolds with sec ⩾ 1 \sec\geqslant 1 and spherical rank at least d − 2 > 0 d-2>0 . Conjecturally, all such manifolds are locally isometric to a round sphere or complex projective space with the (symmetric) Fubini–Study metric.

arxiv-1908-00788.title: Deformable Medical Image Registration Using a Randomly-Initialized CNN as Regularization Prior
arxiv-1908-00788.creator: Max-Heinrich Laves, Sontje Ihler, Tobias Ortmaier
arxiv-1908-00788.description: Abstract We present deformable unsupervised medical image registration using a randomly-initialized deep convolutional neural network (CNN) as regularization prior. Conventional registration methods predict a transformation by minimizing dissimilarities between an image pair. The minimization is usually regularized with manually engineered priors, which limits the potential of the registration.

arxiv-2101-03132.title: Incompatible bounded category forcing axioms Thanks: The first author acknowledges support of EPSRC Grant EP/N032160/1. The second author acknowledges support of GNSAGA. Parts of this research was partially done whilst the authors were visiting fellows at the Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical
arxiv-2101-03132.creator: David Asperó, Matteo Viale
arxiv-2101-03132.description: Abstract . We introduce bounded category forcing axioms for well-behaved classes Γ \Gamma . These are strong forms of bounded forcing axioms which completely decide the theory of some initial segment of the universe H λ Γ + H_{\lambda_{\Gamma}^{+}} modulo forcing in Γ \Gamma , for some cardinal λ Γ \lambda_{\Gamma} naturally associated to Γ \Gamma .

arxiv-2107-05895.title: A Theory of Spherical Diagrams
arxiv-2107-05895.creator: Giovanni Viglietta
arxiv-2107-05895.description: Abstract We introduce an axiomatic theory of spherical diagrams as a tool to study certain combinatorial properties of polyhedra in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} , which are of central interest in the context of Art Gallery problems for polyhedra and other visibility-related problems in discrete and computational geometry. Department of Computer Science and Engineering, University of Aizu, Japan and http://giovanniviglietta.com/ viglietta@gmail.comhttps://orcid.

arxiv-2111-07108.title: On Strominger space forms Thanks: Zheng is partially supported by National Natural Science Foundations of China with the grant No.12071050 and 12141101, Chongqing grant cstc2021ycjh-bgzxm0139, and is supported by the 111 Project D21024.
arxiv-2111-07108.creator: Shuwen Chen, Fangyang Zheng
arxiv-2111-07108.description: Abstract . In this article, we propose the following conjecture: if the Strominger connection of a compact Hermitian manifold has constant non-zero holomorphic sectional curvature, then the Hermitian metric must be Kähler. The main result of this article is to confirm the conjecture in dimension 2 2 .

arxiv-2201-11019.title: Demand Management for Peak to Average Ratio Minimization via Intraday Block Pricing
arxiv-2201-11019.creator: Carolina Cortez, Andreas Kasis, Dimitrios Papadaskalopoulos, Stelios Timotheou
arxiv-2201-11019.description: Abstract Price based demand response schemes may significantly improve power system efficiency. Additionally, it is desired that such schemes yield improved power operation, by reducing the peak consumption. This paper proposes the Intraday Block Pricing (IBP) scheme, aiming to promote effective demand response among consumers by charging their electricity usage based on intraday time-slots.

arxiv-2212-12559.title: Optimizing Staggered Multigrid for Exascale performance
arxiv-2212-12559.creator: Evan Weinberg
arxiv-2212-12559.description: Abstract Adaptive multi-grid methods have proven very successful in dealing with critical slow down for the Wilson-Dirac solver in lattice gauge theory. Multi-grid algorithms developed for Staggered fermions using the Kähler-Dirac preconditioning [ 12 ] have shown remarkable success. In this work, we discuss the performance of this staggered multi-grid algorithm in four dimensions.

arxiv-2304-06338.title: Magnon squeezing in conical spin spirals
arxiv-2304-06338.creator: D. Wuhrer, L. Rózsa, U. Nowak, W. Belzig
arxiv-2304-06338.description: Abstract We investigate squeezing of magnons in a conical spin spiral configuration. We find that while the energy of magnons propagating along the 𝒌 \boldsymbol{k} and the − 𝒌 -\boldsymbol{k} directions can be different due to the non-reciprocal dispersion, these two modes are connected by the squeezing, hence can be described by the same squeezing parameter.

arxiv-2310-13612.title: Fair ω \omega -Regular Games
arxiv-2310-13612.creator: Daniel Hausmann, Nir Piterman, Irmak Sağlam, Anne-Kathrin Schmuck
arxiv-2310-13612.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Daniel Hausmann, Nir Piterman, Irmak Sağlam, Anne-Kathrin Schmuck. arxiv-2311-16351.title: Microscopic Mechanism of the Thermal Amorphization of ZIF-4 and Melting of ZIF-zni Revealed via Molecular Dynamics and Machine Learning Techniques
arxiv-2311-16351.creator: Emilio Mendez, Rocio Semino
arxiv-2311-16351.description: Abstract We investigate the microscopic mechanism of the thermally induced ambient pressure ordered–disordered phase transitions of two zeolitic imidazolate frameworks of formula Zn ( C 3 ​ H 3 ​ N 2 ​ ) 2 \text{Zn}\text{(}\text{C}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}}\text{H}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}}\text{N}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}}\text{)}\text{}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} : a porous (ZIF-4) and a dense, non-porous (ZIF-zni) polymorph via a combination of data science and computer simulation approaches.

arxiv-2403-07849.title: Iterative Graph Neural Network Enhancement via Frequent Subgraph Mining of Explanations Thanks: This publication is based on work supported in part by the University of Illinois at Chicago and the National Science Foundation (NSF) award #CNS-1828265 for MRI: Acquisition of a Composable Platform as a
arxiv-2403-07849.creator: Harish G. Naik, Jan Polster, Raj Shekhar, Tamás Horváth, György Turán
arxiv-2403-07849.description: Abstract We formulate an XAI-based model improvement approach for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for node classification, called Explanation Enhanced Graph Learning (EEGL). The goal is to improve predictive performance of GNN using explanations. EEGL is an iterative self-improving algorithm, which starts with a learned “vanilla” GNN, and repeatedly uses frequent subgraph mining to find relevant patterns in explanation subgraphs.

arxiv-2404-00793.title: Learning the mechanisms of network growth
arxiv-2404-00793.creator: Lourens Touwen, Doina Bucur, Remco van der Hofstad, Alessandro Garavaglia, Nelly Litvak
arxiv-2404-00793.description: Abstract We propose a novel model-selection method for dynamic networks. Our approach involves training a classifier on a large body of synthetic network data. The data is generated by simulating nine state-of-the-art random graph models for dynamic networks, with parameter range chosen to ensure exponential growth of the network size in time.

arxiv-2405-17950.title: Self-Guiding Exploration for Combinatorial Problems
arxiv-2405-17950.creator: Zangir Iklassov, Yali Du, Farkhad Akimov, Martin Takáč
arxiv-2405-17950.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zangir Iklassov, Yali Du, Farkhad Akimov, Martin Takáč. Large Language Models (LLMs) have become pivotal in addressing reasoning tasks across diverse domains, including arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning. They utilize prompting techniques such as Exploration-of-Thought, Decomposition, and Refinement to effectively navigate and solve intricate tasks. Despite these advancements, the application of LLMs to Combinatorial Problems (CPs), known for their NP-hardness and critical roles in logistics and resource management remains underexplored.

arxiv-2505-11081.title: ShiQ : Bringing back Bellman to LLMs
arxiv-2505-11081.creator: Pierre Clavier ‡, Nathan Grinsztajn, Raphael Avalos, Yannis Flet-Berliac, Irem Ergun, Omar D. Domingues, Eugene Tarassov, Olivier Pietquin †, Pierre H. Richemond, Florian Strub, Matthieu Geist †‡
arxiv-2505-11081.description: Abstract The fine-tuning of pre-trained large language models (LLMs) using reinforcement learning (RL) is generally formulated as direct policy optimization. This approach was naturally favored as it efficiently improves a pretrained LLM, seen as an initial policy. Another RL paradigm, Q-learning methods, has received far less attention in the LLM community while demonstrating major success in various non-LLM RL tasks.

arxiv-2509-05804.title: Genetic optimization of ansatz expressibility for enhanced variational quantum algorithm performance
arxiv-2509-05804.creator: Manish Mallapur, Ronit Raj, Ankur Raina
arxiv-2509-05804.description: Abstract Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a leading paradigm that extracts practical computation from near-term intermediate-scale quantum devices, enabling advances in quantum chemistry simulations, combinatorial optimization, and quantum machine learning. However, the performance of Variational Quantum Algorithms is highly sensitive to the design of the ansatze.

arxiv-2509-21419.title: Overview of ExpertLifeCLEF 2018: how far automated identification systems are from the best experts?
arxiv-2509-21419.creator: Hervé Goëau, Pierre Bonnet, Alexis Joly
arxiv-2509-21419.description: Abstract Automated identification of plants and animals has improved considerably in the last few years, in particular thanks to the recent advances in deep learning. The next big question is how far such automated systems are from the human expertise.

arxiv-2510-06494.title: Ensemble seismic study of the properties of the core of Red Clump stars
arxiv-2510-06494.creator: Anthony Noll, Sarbani Basu, and Saskia Hekker
arxiv-2510-06494.description: Abstract Context. Red clump (RC) stars still pose open questions regarding several physical processes, such as the mixing around the core, or the nuclear reactions, which are ill-constrained by theory and experiments. The oscillations of red clump stars, which are of mixed gravito-acoustic nature, allow us to directly investigate the interior of these stars and thereby better understand their physics.

arxiv-2601-14001.title: Auditory Brain Passage Retrieval: Cross-Sensory EEG Training for Neural Information Retrieval
arxiv-2601-14001.creator: Niall McGuire, Yashar Moshfeghi
arxiv-2601-14001.description: Abstract Query formulation from internal information needs remains fundamentally challenging across all Information Retrieval paradigms due to cognitive complexity and physical impairments. Brain Passage Retrieval (BPR) addresses this by directly mapping EEG signals to passage representations without intermediate text translation.

arxiv-2604-05675.title: The final version of a recent approach towards quantum foundation
arxiv-2604-05675.creator: Inge S. Helland, Department of Mathematics. University of Oslo

pmc-10909106.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Immunohistochemistry for HER2-Positive Breast Cancer
pmc-10909106.creator: Siwaporn Thanasan, Kweekrong Sukhakul, Sakchai Chitpakdee, Nakarin Kitkumthorn
pmc-10909106.description: Objective:Currently, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer cells are diagnosed under the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) and College of American Pathologists (CAP) 2018 guidelines. The guideline combined the results of in situ hybridization (DISH) and immunohistochemistry (IHC) techniques. The IHC technique is easy, cheap, and suitable for developing country.

pmc-11499417.title: From Industry 5.0 to Forestry 5.0: Bridging the gap with Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
pmc-11499417.creator: Andreas Holzinger, Janine Schweier, Christoph Gollob, Arne Nothdurft, Hubert Hasenauer, Thomas Kirisits, Carola Häggström, Rien Visser, Raffaele Cavalli, Raffaele Spinelli, Karl Stampfer
pmc-11499417.description: Purpose of the ReviewRecent technological innovations in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have successfully revolutionized many industrial processes, enhancing productivity and sustainability, under the paradigm of Industry 5.0. It offers opportunities for the forestry sector such as predictive analytics, automation, and precision management, which could transform traditional forest operations into smart, effective, and sustainable practices.

pmc-11637370.title: Racial differences and geographic variations in oral anticoagulation treatment among Medicare patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation
pmc-11637370.creator: Larry R. Jackson, Amiee Kang, Virginia Noxon, Nipun Atreja, Dionne M. Hines, Melissa Hagan, Jenny Jiang, Brett D. Atwater
pmc-11637370.description: IntroductionUse of oral anticoagulants (OACs) for stroke reduction in atrial fibrillation (AF) varies by race and geography within the United States. We seek to better understand the relationship between OAC underutilization, race, and US geography.MethodsPatients with AF were selected from the US Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services claims database from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2016.

pmc-12470943.title: Novel Organomineral Complex with Prolonged Antitumor Action
pmc-12470943.creator: Olga Ilinskaya, Galina Yakovleva, Pavel Zelenikhin, Alexey Kolpakov, William Kurdy, Mikhail Glukhov, Igor Sedov, Sergey Kharintsev
pmc-12470943.description: Blocking the MAPK pathway is a strategy to stop cancer cells proliferation. Despite all the successes, the acquisition of drug resistance by cells, as well as the mutational status of the downstream protein KRAS, reduces the tumor response to therapy. Ribonuclease binase from Bacillus pumilus is among the agents that block this pathway through direct interaction with EGFR and RAS.

pmc-12557868.creator: Ahmed Amir Samir, Ahmed Samy Elgammal, Abdelrhman Mahmoud Alieldeen, Eman Gomaa Allam, Imen ketata, Emna Ellouz, Rawan Gameel Hekal, Hossam Salameh, Nasrouha Didda, Naima Kebir, Abderrhman Abdelfattah Selim, Hussein Zeyad Atshan, Aiman Awad Bashir, Riad Azzam Kouzeiha, Hanadi Alayiab, Ibrahim Ali Ka

BackgroundMigraine is a prevalent and debilitating neurological condition that significantly impact the academic lives of university students. pmc-12954348.title: Real‐World Analysis of Outcomes of Venetoclax+Azacitidine Versus 7+3 Induction in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
pmc-12954348.creator: Nehemias Guevara Rodriguez, Noemy Coreas Mercado, Syeda Ashna Fatima Kamal, Sandeep Beesabathina, Dawson Foster, Nabeel Rajeh, Ranju Kunwor
pmc-12954348.description: BackgroundVenetoclax plus azacitidine (V+A) is standard for older, intensive‐ineligible patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Its expanding use in younger, curative‐eligible adults lacks comparative evidence against conventional 7+3 induction, raising uncertainty about potential survival compromise.MethodsWe performed an age‐stratified, retrospective comparative effectiveness study using de‐identified TriNetX electronic health records (2018–2025).

pmc-13000633.title: Production of 5‑Hydroxymethylfurfural from Glucose under Hydrothermal Conditions
pmc-13000633.creator: Haojie Tian, Sichan Li, Mengli Zhou, Tingyu Zhu, Xinyu Liu, Zhimin Wu, Qiying Liu, Jianchun Jiang
pmc-13000633.description: 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) is an important biomass-based platform molecule with various commercial applications, and its green, efficient production is the key for value-added applications of lignocellulosic biomass. This work studied the preparation of 5-HMF from glucose using autogenic H+ and OH– as the catalysts under hydrothermal conditions without additional catalysts.

pmc-13138871.title: Atimiaphobia: The Undiscovered Burden of Honor Cultures and Shame Societies on Mental Health—Development and Validation of Atimiaphobia Scale
pmc-13138871.creator: Waqar Husain, Muhammad Ahmad Husain, Farrukh Ijaz, Khaled Trabelsi, Achraf Ammar, Haitham Jahrami
pmc-13138871.description: The psychological impact of honor cultures and shame societies on the general population has not been examined through a diagnostic lens. Atimiaphobia is a newly recognized psychological condition characterized by an intense fear of losing honor or being labeled shameless, deeply rooted in honor cultures and shame societies.

pmc-13387956.title: Robotic Approach to Right-Sided Hiatal Hernia Involving the Ascending and Transverse Colon, Duodenum, and Distal Stomach: A Case Report
pmc-13387956.creator: Woo Jun Kim, Dongwon Lim, Joohyung Son, Bong Soo Son, Si-Hak Lee, Sun-Hwi Hwang, Jae Hun Chung
pmc-13387956.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). INTRODUCTIONCases of hiatal hernia (HH) involving the distal stomach, duodenum, and ascending and transverse colon are exceptionally rare and present significant surgical challenges owing to severe anatomical distortion. Although minimally invasive surgery is the gold standard for HH repair, the application of a robotic approach to this specific complex configuration involving distal gastric and duodenal herniations has not been previously reported.

pmc-13473558.title: Electron tomography reveals mitochondrial network and cristae remodelling during cell differentiation in the human placenta
pmc-13473558.creator: Siddharth Acharya, Eric Hanssen, Veronica B. Botha, Tia M. Smith, Sahan Jayatissa, Zlatan Trifunovic, Lucy A. Bartho, John E. Schjenken, Tu’uhevaha J. Kaitu’u-Lino, Anthony V. Perkins, Joanna L. James, Kirsty G. Pringle, James C. Bouwer, Roger Smith, Joshua J. Fisher
pmc-13473558.description: Mitochondria adapt their structure through fusion and fission, yet how their morphology and cristae architecture change as cells differentiate remains unclear. The human placenta is a valuable model for studying mitochondrial diversity within a single tissue. As epithelial trophoblast cells of the placenta differentiate, their accompanying mitochondria morphologically and functionally transform.

pmc-13654159.title: Apparent diffusion coefficient histogram parameters of the whole tumor based on whole-body magnetic resonance imaging can better characterize the tumor burden of multiple myeloma and predict survival prognosis
pmc-13654159.creator: Huazheng Dong, Qingyan Qi, Xiaodong Ji, Shanshan Gao, Kemin Zhang, Song Liu, Zhiyi Song, Wenyang Huang, Shuang Xia
pmc-13654159.description: BackgroundNewly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) is characterized by a spatially heterogeneous tumor burden. Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WB-MRI)-derived apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) histogram analysis may enable comprehensive characterization of tumor burden. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility of using whole-tumor ADC histogram parameters based on WB-MRI images to assess tumor burden and evaluate their prognostic value in NDMM patients.
